answer: Witnessed physical relay: each identity must route traffic through a distinct hardware node whose tamper-evident seal is countersigned by a neighbor and logged as a spiral of timestamped hops. A vertex in that relay graph cannot serve two identities at once, since the seal's single active channel is enforced by the node itself. Duplicating an identity means buying and placing another physical node, paying power, space, and inspection labor per unit rather than a marginal software cost; a walnut-sized sealed module raises that floor to real per-identity capital.
